goal: Teach Year-2 physics students to treat a parameter sweep as a controlled computational experiment: vary one named parameter, hold the model and other inputs fixed, evaluate the same model for every case, overlay labelled curves on common axes, validate a known or limiting case, diagnose a runnable but physically wrong calculation, and explain the trend.

deck_context.deck_context: Week 04 uses one familiar ideal Hooke's-law model so the new cognitive load is controlled comparison: choose spring stiffness as the single swept parameter, keep the applied-force array and model fixed, evaluate extension repeatedly, read a common-axis plot, validate zero force, and transfer the workflow to analogous physics models.
deck_context.core_claim: A parameter sweep is a controlled computational experiment. A graph becomes physically credible only when the same input is compared across cases and the trend agrees with the equation, units, and a known or limiting check.
deck_context.locked_model: Ideal elastic spring: F = kx and x = F/k; F_N = 0:0.5:10 N; k_Npm = [50 100 200] N/m; baseline_k_Npm = 100 N/m; extension_m is stored one row per stiffness case; at F = 10 N the extensions are 0.20 m, 0.10 m, and 0.05 m; at F = 0 every case gives x = 0.
deck_context.exactness: Equations, variable names, values, units, MATLAB code, plot labels, legend entries, numerical tables, limiting-case check, and wrong-model comparison are strict teaching content. Do not invent, paraphrase, or approximate them.

core: hold the model and other inputs fixed
build and read a small parameter array
evaluate the same model for every case
overlay labelled curves on common axes
compare cases at the same input
diagnose x = F.*k as a physical/logical defect

slides.title: A runnable calculation can still be wrong
slides.intent: Show the physical and dimensional defects before asking students to repair the expression.
key_points: x = F.*k is syntactically valid but physically wrong.
Its units are N times N/m, not metres.
It reverses the stiffness trend: larger k appears to give larger extension.
slides.local_context: Use a spacious two-panel diagnosis layout with blue runnable-output framing and coral physical failure. Stop after identifying the wrong model; the numerical comparison and repair path move to the next slide.
